category_fits.label: Consumer Behavior & Insights
category_fits.why_fit: The report's central focus is how consumers think, feel, choose, and shop: it examines value perceptions, deal-seeking, brand switching, trust, spending, AI-assisted shopping, and human interaction, based on a global survey of 12,000 consumers.
evidence_sections: Value redefined: where fairness and quality intersect
Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries
supported_topic_rules: The report repeatedly studies consumer attitudes, motivations, trust, decision drivers, and behavioral shifts.
Consumer behavior is the core subject and the report remains useful without a business-performance or media lens.
rule_evidence_sections: Value redefined: where fairness and quality intersect
Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries
centrality_evidence_sections: Value redefined: where fairness and quality intersect

category_fits.label: Agentic Commerce & Shopping Automation
category_fits.why_fit: The AI section reports that 52% use virtual assistants weekly for tasks such as reordering or meal planning, and that consumers want rules controlling when assistants act.
category_fits.why_not_fit: AI-assisted shopping is one major topic within a broader consumer-expectations report; the report is not mainly about agents executing shopping, purchase, or checkout flows.
evidence_sections: Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries
supported_topic_rules: The report connects assistants and automation with shopping-related tasks such as reordering.

category_fits.label: AI & Automation
category_fits.why_fit: The report discusses virtual assistants, generative-AI recommendations, and consumer control over assistant actions.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Its main lens is consumer attitudes and shopping behavior, not AI systems or automation as a general capability across tasks, teams, or systems.
evidence_sections: Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries
supported_topic_rules: The report discusses AI assistants and generative-AI-enabled shopping experiences.
rule_evidence_sections: Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries

category_fits.label: Omnichannel Commerce
category_fits.why_fit: The report discusses online deal-seeking, social-media purchases, retail-channel trust, and in-store human support.
category_fits.why_not_fit: These are consumer findings across shopping contexts; the report does not make coordinated online-and-offline commerce experience or end-to-end touchpoint integration its main subject.
evidence_sections: Value redefined: where fairness and quality intersect
Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries

category_fits.label: Privacy, Identity & Data
category_fits.why_fit: The report notes that consumers assess data privacy when judging retail-channel trust and discusses comfort with sharing shopping history for personalization.
category_fits.why_not_fit: Privacy is a trust consideration within a wider consumer report, not its core problem; the context does not focus on identity, consent systems, compliance, or privacy-safe data design.
evidence_sections: Value redefined: where fairness and quality intersect
Reliable tech builds loyalty – but with boundaries
rejected_topic_rules: Privacy is a constraint mentioned within a broader consumer and AI report rather than the report's central subject.
rule_evidence_sections: Value redefined: where fairness and quality intersect

category_fits.label: Digital Payments & Wallets
category_fits.why_fit: The report mentions secure payments as one factor consumers consider when assessing retail-channel trust.
category_fits.why_not_fit: It does not examine payment products, wallet adoption, checkout friction, payment preferences, or payment security as a central business problem.
evidence_sections: Value redefined: where fairness and quality intersect
rejected_topic_rules: Payments are a minor trust consideration within a broader consumer report.
